subject: Forensic sampling & data-handling guidance during latency incident
messages:
From: Lina Torres <lina@velocitech.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@velocitech.com
Date: 2026-08-29T08:12:00Z
Subject: Severe error-rate spike — request for evidence and PII scope

Hi Jasmine,

We're seeing sustained 5xx errors and a throughput drop during our peak window this morning (08:00–08:40 UTC). Our compliance team needs a small set of artifacts for an internal postmortem and evidence for our auditor:

- A 30-minute sample of runtime logs and request/response metadata around 08:00–08:30 UTC
- Confirmation whether any responses included customer PII fields (names, emails, SSNs) and guidance on redaction
- A short note on retention window for those logs and any exportable audit trail

Can you provide this as a secure package (or point us to a secure share)? We need to present this at a 10:30 internal meeting. Please escalate as needed — this is impacting our customer SLAs.

Thanks,
Lina
Lead Ops, Velocitech
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina@velocitech.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T08:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Severe error-rate spike — request for evidence and PII scope

Hi Lina — thanks for flagging and apologies for the disruption. We're on it.

Quick clarifying Qs so we scope the evidence package correctly:
- For the 30-minute window, do you want the full request/response payloads or just headers/metadata + error traces?
- Is redaction required before we hand anything to you, or is it acceptable to deliver raw artifacts to your secure share with a signed chain-of-custody?

I'm looping in Marcus (runtime) and Rachel (security/compliance) to propose the minimal artifact set and delivery method. Expect an internal plan in ~45–60 minutes; we'll aim to have a secure share link before your 10:30 meeting.

— Jasmine

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T08:35:00Z
Subject: ACTION: Velocitech evidence package — scope & chain-of-custody

Team — Velocitech needs a tight evidence bundle for a compliance review after a latency/error spike. Lina asked for 08:00–08:30 UTC artifacts. Requirements: minimal set, rapid turnaround, and auditable chain-of-custody. Key constraints from customer: they will present to auditors at 10:30 (in two hours).

Please propose:
- exact artifacts we can deliver (log types, sampling strategy, anonymization/redaction steps)
- filename conventions and a short README describing collection steps (chain of custody)
- where we'll stage the package (secure Drive share or SFTP) and who signs off internally

Cc: Stephanie for legal/comms if we need a short signed statement about retention policy. I'll own external communication.

Thanks — Jasmine
From: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: ACTION: Velocitech evidence package — scope & chain-of-custody

Plan and artifacts (rapid deliverable):

1) Artifacts we'll produce (minimal, redaction-first):
   - runtime_snippets_08-29-2026.tar.gz (gzip of sequential 1s-resolution runtime traces for 07:55–08:35 UTC: includes timestamps, node id, model variant, token counts)
   - kv_cache_sample_20260829.jsonl (sampled KV-cache entries with keys hashed, values replaced with length metadata)
   - error_traces_08-29_0800-0830.log (HTTP/GRPC stack traces with request-ids)
   - chain_of_custody_readme.txt (collection timestamps, exporter hostnames, operator names, cryptographic hash of archive)

2) PII handling:
   - We do not retain customer PII in logs except for short-lived request/response payloads when customers send it. For this account, we will scan the payloads for probable PII patterns (emails, SSNs, creditcard-like numbers) and redact values prior to packaging. Redaction process: deterministic regex -> replace with <REDACTED:TYPE> and record counts in README. Any suspicious items will be flagged to Rachel for review.

3) Sampling & scope:
   - We'll deliver full payloads only for error requests (5xx) in the 08:00–08:30 window; for non-error requests we provide metadata only. This keeps package small and meets their ask.

4) Chain-of-custody and signing:
   - I'll generate SHA256 hashes for each artifact and place them in chain_of_custody_readme.txt.
   - Delivery via a time-limited, audit-logged Drive folder (link below); only named Velocitech contacts will be granted access.

5) ETA: initial package ready by 10:00 UTC (packs will be uploaded, hashes published). If Stephanie or Rachel want legal wording, we can attach a short statement signed by Security.

Attachments (placeholders): runtime_snippets_08-29-2026.tar.gz, kv_cache_sample_20260829.jsonl, chain_of_custody_readme.txt

— Marcus
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Lina — quick update and delivery plan.

What we're delivering (secure link below):
- runtime_snippets_08-29-2026.tar.gz (sequential runtime traces; non-PII payloads redacted)
- kv_cache_sample_20260829.jsonl (keys hashed, values length-masked)
- error_traces_08-29_0800-0830.log (5xx request traces)
- chain_of_custody_readme.txt (hashes + extraction steps + operator signatures)

Notes:

- Retention: these runtime traces are retained per your contract for 30 days by default; after delivery we can arrange either (a) to snapshot and delete from our short-term store, or (b) leave them in our secure audit bucket for 90 days if you request it and sign a short order.

Secure download: https://drive.redwood.example/incident/velocitech/4821 (time-limited link, audit logs enabled)
JIRA reference: JIRA-INC-4821

If you want a signed statement from Security about our procedures and the hashes, Rachel can attach one — we can produce that within 2 hrs. Please confirm if the above works for your auditor.

Thanks,
Jasmine
